doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sarah Vaughan's trio, arrangements and personnel
summary: With Europe and recording came the freedom to build parts in a loose trio with Joe Benjamin, Jimmy Jones, John Malachi and Ronnell Bright.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: So then Sarah basically is where you got to go to Europe . . .
That was the first time I went to Europe, yeah.
. . . did extensive recording, lots of different contexts for your musical . . .
Yeah, yeah. That was enjoyable too.
How about getting along with musical directors and having to put up with conductors? What was that relationship like?

We didn’t have to deal with that, because the conductors would be out of the band. It wouldn’t be – it would either be Jimmy Jones, or John Malachi was the other at first. Jimmy had studied conducting. I was free to – we had a tight trio, because we would take the arrangements – the big-band arrangements – and make – they would just grow into arrangements. They got pretty intricate without somebody saying, “Here’s a part.” It was just loose enough to make your own part, and it really happened.
So you were composing your own parts in these arrangements.

That’s right. Just around the arrangement itself, adding to it and putting other things. It’s some very interesting stuff that was loose and then we could vary on it a little bit. You know what I mean?

It was Joe Benjamin at first and John Malachi. Then Jimmy Jones had come back, because he was sick for a while. Then when he left, I think Ronnell Bright. Then Joe had an automobile accident. I think Richard Davis had come in. Then when Ronnell Bright came in, it started changing, going in another . . .
